gaps.sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: One of the bolts had worked ___ in the vibration.
gaps.explanation: 'Work loose' = become untightened; 'lose' is the verb for misplacing.

gaps.sentence: We sat ___ to the sound of the waves.
gaps.explanation: 'Listen to' means to pay attention to sound deliberately; after 'sat' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: Unemployment has ___ sharply since the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Has risen' — rise does not take an object.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.
